name: device-comparator-flicker-noise
description: Input-referred noise density and flicker corner for the 3.3 V comparator input candidates, at both gf180mcu flicker-noise corner settings (fnoicor 0 and 1) plus a flicker-disabled thermal reference, over the full PVT matrix.
claim: None yet — device characterization ahead of a ratified spec line (#1). Feeds #9 (comparator noise budget and input-pair sizing).

fc_n_hz.description: flicker corner of the NMOS pair candidate at 10 uA, fnoicor = 0. Extracted as the crossing of the measured 1/f asymptote with the separately measured thermal-only floor: fc = (V_n(1 Hz) / V_n,thermal)^2.

flicker_area_ratio.description: V_n(1 Hz) of the 40/0.5 device divided by V_n(1 Hz) of the 40/2.0 device at identical current. Flicker noise power goes as 1/(W*L), so 4x the gate area must halve the noise AMPLITUDE: this must land near 2.0. It is the measured evidence for the area scaling #9 will use to trade input-pair area against flicker noise, and it fails loudly if the models ever stop scaling.

fnoicor_power_ratio_n.description: worst-case / as-extracted flicker noise POWER for the NMOS, measured. It must reproduce the model card's own noia ratio, 3.5e42 / 3.2e41 = 10.94 — which simultaneously proves that the alterparam+reset flicker-corner switch in this manifest actually takes effect. If this check ever passes at 1.0, the worst-case half of this record is not worst case.

fnoicor_power_ratio_p.description: same for the PMOS, whose model card ratio is 4.0e42 / 3.2e41 = 12.5.

vn_n_th_nv.description: thermal-only input-referred noise density of the NMOS pair candidate, measured with every BSIM flicker term zeroed (fnoicor = 2, see notes). It goes as sqrt(4kT*gamma/gm), so the temperature axis must move it and the process axis must move it through gm. The band is a plausibility guard for a ~200 uS device. The process floor is 1 %, not the 3 % a MOS-corner check usually gets, and deliberately so: at a FIXED drain current gm moves only ~4 % across the five MOS corners (see sim/device-comparator-gm-id/, gmid_n_pair), and thermal noise is its square root, so ~2 % is the whole physically available signal and the weakest grid slice gives 1.3 %. The floor's job here is to prove the process axis is live at all -- it collapses to 0 % under --sabotage-corners -- not to assert a large movement.

th_flatness_n.description: the flicker-disabled spectrum's 1 Hz value divided by its 1 MHz value. White noise is flat, so this must be 1.000. It is the proof that fnoicor = 2 really does switch every flicker term off, which is what licenses vn_*_th_nv to be used as the thermal reference in the fc_* extractions.

flicker_slope_pow_dec.description: measured power-law exponent of the low-frequency spectrum between 1 Hz and 1 kHz, in decades of noise POWER per decade of frequency. Ideal 1/f gives exactly 1.0. This is what makes the fc_* extraction legitimate: those numbers assume a 1/f asymptote, and this check is the evidence that the assumption holds over the band where it is applied.

evidence.data_provenance: simulated — gf180mcu ngspice device models (sm141064.ngspice nfet_03v3 / pfet_03v3 subckts and the PDK's own `noise_corner` section), over the harness's five MOS process corners, at both settings of the PDK's fnoicor flicker-noise corner switch. No foundry datasheet or literature value is involved.
notes: inoise_spectrum is in V/sqrt(Hz). This was confirmed independently against an ideal 1 kOhm resistor, which ngspice reports as 4.069 nV/sqrt(Hz) against the 4kTR value of 4.07 nV/sqrt(Hz). Every vn_* number below is therefore an amplitude density, and every fc_* and *_power_ratio_* number squares it into a power ratio before use.

FLICKER CORNER DEFINITION AND ITS THERMAL REFERENCE. fc is extracted as the crossing of the measured 1/f asymptote with a separately MEASURED thermal floor: fc = (V_n(1 Hz) / V_n,thermal)^2. The thermal floor is not read off the high-frequency end of the spectrum -- the diode-connected node's own pole (gm/2*pi*C, a few hundred MHz here) distorts the input-referred density well before it settles, so a high-frequency asymptote would be an artefact. Instead the whole sweep is repeated a third time with every BSIM flicker term zeroed. That is done by setting fnoicor = 2: the PDK writes noia/noib/noic as '(fnoicor==0)*<typ> + (fnoicor==1)*<worst>', so any other code makes all three terms exactly zero. th_flatness_n checks that the resulting spectrum really is white (1 Hz value / 1 MHz value = 1.000), so this is a verified null control rather than a trick.

fnoicor is the PDK's own flicker-noise corner switch (design.ngspice): 0 = as-extracted (its default), 1 = worst case. Both are run at every PVT point via alterparam + reset. #9 must state which setting any quoted noise number came from; the worst-case setting raises flicker noise POWER by 10.9x (NMOS) / 12.5x (PMOS) and leaves the thermal floor essentially untouched.

Devices are diode-connected at Vds = Vgs, i.e. at the edge of saturation. A real comparator input pair runs at higher Vds and will show a slightly different gm; the noise DENSITY referred to the gate is dominated by gm and by gate area, both of which are reported here.

This is a small-signal noise density, not a comparator noise budget: sampled-system noise folding, the regeneration-time-dependent noise bandwidth of a dynamic latch, and kickback are all #9's job. What this record supplies is the device-level input to that calculation.
